description: Replace the tower planner's 'weakest viable team' logic with real-opponent-power, margin-aware selection. Fetches actual enemy teams from /game/v1/nodeCombats/{combatId}, allocates scarce strong characters to the hardest cells first, surfaces honest confidence and margin signals, and captures post-fight outcomes for personal-margin tuning.

userStories.title: Enemy team fetcher for tower cells
userStories.description: As the tower planner, I need a module that fetches and caches the real enemy team for any tower cell so downstream solver and UI code has accurate opponent data.
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/lib/tower-enemy-fetcher.ts exports getEnemyTeam(combatId, towerId) and getEnemyTeamsForRooms(rooms, towerId)
Calls /game/v1/nodeCombats/{combatId}?charInfo=full&difficulty=0&difficultyGroup={towerId} via existing msfApiFetch helper in src/lib/msf-api.ts
Returns typed EnemyTeam { combatId, units: EnemyUnit[], totalPower: number } where EnemyUnit includes id, name, level, gearTier, activeYellow, activeRed, power, stats, nodeEffects, iso8
Skips rooms with no combatId; returns null for those entries in the array form
In-memory cache keyed by combatId, invalidated when meta.hashes.nodes changes (mirrors checkHashInvalidation pattern in src/lib/dd-service.ts)
Unit tests in src/lib/tower-enemy-fetcher.test.ts cover: successful fetch, missing combatId, cache hit, cache invalidation on hash change
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented src/lib/tower-enemy-fetcher.ts with getEnemyTeam / getEnemyTeamsForRooms, in-memory cache keyed by combatId, node-hash invalidation mirroring dd-service.ts. 4 unit tests passing; typecheck + lint clean.

userStories.title: Solve API exposes opponent power per room
userStories.description: As the tower planner client, I need the /api/tower/solve route to include real opponent power per room in its response so the UI and solver work from the same numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: src/app/api/tower/solve/route.ts handler calls getEnemyTeamsForRooms for the active tower's room list
Response JSON adds opponentPowers: Record<string, number> (roomId -> total opponent power) and opponentTeams: Record<string, EnemyTeam>
Existing response fields are preserved; no breaking changes to fields already consumed by TowerPlannerClient
Per-room fetch failures degrade gracefully: response includes successful rooms plus a roomFetchErrors: string[] listing failed combatIds
Unit test in src/app/api/tower/solve/route.test.ts mocks the fetcher and asserts opponentPowers, opponentTeams, and roomFetchErrors appear with correct values
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Margin-aware team selection in tower-solver
userStories.description: As a commander, I want the solver to pick the lowest-power eligible team that still beats the opponent by a safety margin so I save my best characters for the hardest cells without recommending death squads.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/tower-solver.ts solveTowerAllocation accepts new opponentPowers: Map<string, number> and safetyMargin: number (default 1.10) options
For each room, after meetsRequirements filtering, eligible characters are sorted ascending by power and the smallest contiguous prefix whose summed power >= opponentPower * safetyMargin is selected
When no eligible subset meets the margin, solver picks the strongest eligible team (descending sort, take top N) and tags that room's result with marginFallback: true
Rooms processed in descending opponentPower order so scarce strong characters are reserved for the hardest cells
Exports a named constant SAFETY_MARGIN_DEFAULT = 1.10

Three new tests in src/lib/tower-solver.test.ts: (a) comfortable margin selects mid-power team not weakest, (b) no-viable-margin falls back to strongest with marginFallback: true, (c) ordering reserves top characters for the highest-opponentPower room
All previously-passing tests in tower-solver.test.ts still pass (update expected outputs only where the new logic legitimately changes them)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: This is the core behavior fix. Depends on US-001 type for opponentPowers shape.

userStories.title: Honest confidence score from real margin
userStories.description: As a commander reading a recommendation, I want the confidence label and reason to reflect the team's margin over the actual opponent, not a self-referential calculation.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/tower-solver.ts getConfidence(teamPower, opponentPower) returns one of 'strong' | 'shouldWork' | 'risky' | 'likelyLoss' using thresholds: >=1.30 strong, 1.10-1.30 shouldWork, 0.95-1.10 risky, <0.95 likelyLoss
Each result object includes marginPct (rounded to nearest integer) and a one-line reason string referencing the margin (e.g. 'Your team is ~18% stronger than the opponent.')
The previous self-referential baselineEstimate = minCharPower * 5 logic is removed
Old call sites that pass only teamPower keep compiling via a deprecated overload that delegates with opponentPower = teamPower / 1.10
Unit tests cover all four thresholds and the boundary values (1.30, 1.10, 0.95)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: UI shows opponent power, team power, margin, confidence per cell
userStories.description: As a commander using the planner, I want each room card to show the real opponent power, my team's power, the margin percentage, and the new confidence chip so I can see why a recommendation is or isn't safe.
acceptanceCriteria: src/app/(app)/analyze/tower-planner/TowerPlannerClient.tsx renders for each room: opponent power, team total power, margin % (color-coded: green >=25%, yellow 10-25%, red <10%, deep-red <0%), and confidence chip including the new likelyLoss state
Cards with marginFallback: true show a visible warning banner using the existing destructive alert style: 'No team meets the recommended {margin}x safety margin - best available shown.'
Rooms whose enemy fetch failed (present in roomFetchErrors) show a muted 'Opponent data unavailable' line and silently use legacy entry-requirement-based selection
New e2e spec e2e/tower-planner-difficulty.spec.ts asserts the margin % renders on at least one room card and the warning banner renders when forced into fallback mode (via test fixture / mock)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002 (API response shape) and US-004 (confidence return shape).

userStories.title: User-tunable safety margin slider
userStories.description: As a commander, I want a header slider to dial my safety margin up or down across the whole tower without re-fetching data.
acceptanceCriteria: Slider in the TowerPlannerClient header, range 1.00-1.50, step 0.05, default 1.10, labeled 'Safety margin'
Changing the slider re-runs the client-side solve against already-fetched opponentPowers/opponentTeams - no new API calls
Value persists in localStorage keyed by `tower-planner-margin:${towerEventId}`; clears when towerEventId changes
A 'Reset to default' link next to the slider snaps the value back to 1.10
Unit test covers the persistence read/write helper (pure function)
E2E test covers slider interaction triggering a margin recompute on at least one room card
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Depends on US-005 (UI surface in place).

userStories.title: Post-fight outcome feedback and suggested personal margin
userStories.description: As a commander, after I run a fight I want to mark Won easily / Won barely / Lost so future runs suggest a personal safety margin based on my actual outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Each room card renders three small buttons: 'Won easily', 'Won barely', 'Lost'
Clicking a button stores { towerEventId, roomId, outcome, recommendedTeam, opponentPower, timestamp } in localStorage under key 'tower-planner-outcomes' (rolling list)
A rolling tally of the last 20 outcomes computes a suggested personal margin displayed next to the safety-margin slider, e.g. 'Suggested: 1.20x - your last 10 fights at 1.10x lost 30% of the time.'
Suggestion is informational only - it never auto-changes the slider value
Unit tests cover outcome storage, rolling-window math, and the suggestion-text generator (pure functions)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Node-effect-aware opponent power adjustment
userStories.description: As a commander, I want per-character node buffs (extra hp/dmg/armor on specific tower nodes) to be reflected in the displayed opponent power so buffed cells aren't underweighted.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/tower-enemy-fetcher.ts exports applyNodeEffects(unit) that multiplies unit.power by 1 + sum(boosts) / 1000 (boosts CSV is health,damage,armor,focus,resist in tenths of a percent)
EnemyTeam.totalPower reflects the adjusted values for every unit
Unit test verifies (a) an unboosted unit's adjusted power equals its base power and (b) a unit with boosts '350,150,50,25,25' has adjusted power higher than base by the expected ratio within +-2%
Code comment documents this as a heuristic pending dev clarification on Q1 (difficulty scaling)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
